Meshed text

Source: R/text.R
lari_text.Rd

Shape a string, take its glyph outlines and mesh them: the one-call form of lari_text_outline() followed by lari_glyphs(). Needs the 'textshaping' and 'systemfonts' packages.

Usage

lari_text(
  text,
  family = "",
  weight = "normal",
  italic = FALSE,
  path = NULL,
  em = 1,
  tolerance = 0.002,
  ...
)

Arguments

text

a character string (newlines start new lines)

family, weight, italic, path

font selection, passed to textshaping::shape_text() (path is a font file, which overrides family)

em

the size of one em (the font size) in output units

tolerance

the maximum distance between the flattened outline and the curves of the font, in output units

...

passed to lari_glyphs() and on to lari_triangulate() (max_area, min_angle, size for a sizing field, erase, merge)

Value

see lari_glyphs()

Examples

r <- lari_text("lari", max_area = 0.002, min_angle = 25)
table(r$triangles$glyph)
#> 
#>   1   2   3   4 
#>  62 384 128  42 
tri <- r$triangles
idx <- rbind(tri$v0, tri$v1, tri$v2, NA)
plot(r$vertices$x, r$vertices$y, type = "n", asp = 1, axes = FALSE,
     xlab = "", ylab = "")
polygon(r$vertices$x[idx], r$vertices$y[idx], col = "grey90", border = "grey40")
